title: fix(objectql): work a ctx.api.transaction unit starts and does not await no longer keeps its finished handle
body:
Fixes #22855
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`ctx.api.transaction(fn)` is `ScopedContext.transaction()` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`). When it opened a unit, work the callback started and did not await (an `async: true` hook on a record the callback wrote) kept the unit's handle after the unit finished. Its write then failed with `Transaction query already complete` and was lost. The handle reached that work two ways. Both are now closed when the callback settles, before the commit.

- **Ambient half.** `ScopedContext.transaction()` published `{ transaction, scope }` into the engine's ambient store and never cleared it. PR #22819 had closed the same entry for `engine.transaction()` with an inline `.finally(...)`. That pattern is now ONE helper, `ObjectQL.runOpenedUnit(trx, owner, body)`. Both surfaces run their callback through it. `engine.transaction()`'s ambient behaviour is what PR #22819 shipped; only its body moved into the helper.
- **Explicit half.** The unit's handle is also threaded into the callback's context (`tx.object(...)`, or a caller's `{ context: trx }` from `engine.transaction()`), and from there into the triggered hook's `ctx.api`. Closing the ambient entry does not reach that copy, because `buildDriverOptions` prefers an explicit handle. The helper therefore also records the unit in a `WeakMap` from handle to that same entry (`openedUnits`). `buildDriverOptions`, the one place a context's handle becomes a driver option, treats a handle whose entry is closed as absent (`isClosedUnitHandle`). So the late write runs unenrolled, on its own connection. The write door reads the handle the same way (`opensAfterAbortUnit`), so such a write also opens the door's own unit when its hooks call for one.

One mechanism: the single write that closes the entry answers both reads, the ambient one and the explicit one.

Not changed: work the callback awaits still runs inside the unit and commits or rolls back with it. A joined (nested) unit's handle stays live until the outermost callback settles (pinned). Handles the discrete `beginTransaction` / `commitTransaction` / `rollbackTransaction` trio opens (the QuickJS sandbox path) never pass through the helper and behave as before. A primitive handle cannot key a `WeakMap`, so it keeps the ambient half only. Every in-tree driver returns an object or a function.

## The explicit half: the choice and its alternatives

The dispatch asked for the choice to be stated, because PR #22819's form settles the ambient half only.

- **Chosen: the unit's liveness lives on its entry, and the explicit read consults the same entry.** This is closest to PR #22819: the same closure, reused. It covers every un-awaited reader of a threaded handle, not just hooks. Through the shared helper it also closes the caller-opened `engine.transaction()` explicit half that the card names. That is the one behaviour change `engine.transaction()` gets beyond the extraction. The card and the triage's pins name it, and it needs no edit inside `engine.transaction()` itself.
- **Alternative A: detach fire-and-forget hooks at dispatch** (`hook-wrappers.ts` strips the unit handle from the detached hook's `ctx.api` and leaves the ambient store). Not taken. It is a second mechanism, which the triage rules out. It covers `async: true` hooks only, not other un-awaited work that captured `trxCtx`.
- **Alternative B: stop threading the handle explicitly in `ScopedContext.transaction()`** and rely on the ambient store. Not taken. It changes the explicit-handle contract that `buildDriverOptions` and the joined branch rely on across async boundaries. It cannot cover a caller who threads `engine.transaction()`'s context by hand.

## Landing point

`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, one unit test file under `packages/objectql/src/`, and one changeset. The real-door pin is one test-only file in `packages/qa/dogfood`. The claim declared it conditionally, and the condition held: no real driver is reachable from `packages/objectql`, which has no driver dependency, and its tests use stub drivers. PR #22819's real-door pin lives in the same place.

## Tests

The real-door pin, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/scoped-transaction-late-write.dogfood.test.ts`, runs on the verify stack (sqlite-wasm) through the engine door `hooks.run`, with the card's probe as its shape. A `beforeInsert` handler writes a record inside `ctx.api.transaction`. The record's object carries an `async: true` `afterInsert` hook that writes a note 40 ms later. Four cases:
- the card's probe, with the write through the unit's own context (explicit);
- the same unit, with the write enrolled only ambiently;
- a caller-opened `engine.transaction()` whose handle the write carries explicitly;
- CONTROL: no transaction.

**Before the fix**, on base `0253192f76` with `dist` built from it: 3 failed and 1 passed. The control passed. The three unit cases failed with `expected [ 1, +0 ] to deeply equal [ 1, 1 ]`: the record was stored and the late note was not. knex logged `Transaction query already complete, run with DEBUG=knex:tx for more info`. That is the card's measurement reproduced on a published door.

**After the fix**, at the final head `ec20faf27e` (patch round 1):
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 test/scoped-transaction-late-write.dogfood.test.ts test/hook-after-abort-rollback.dogfood.test.ts`: 2 files, 10 passed. PR #22819's own pins are unchanged.
- The unit layer, `packages/objectql/src/engine-scoped-transaction-late-write.test.ts`, uses a driver whose handle refuses use after commit or rollback, as knex's does. It has the same three cases and the control, plus a joined-unit case: a handle joined through `ctx.api.transaction` inside `engine.transaction()` still enrols after the inner callback settles. Since patch round 1 it also has the door-unit pin and its control: in a closed `ctx.api.transaction` unit, a late write on an object whose blocking default-`onError` `afterInsert` throws opens 1 door unit and rolls back 1, and the note row is absent; with no transaction, the same 1 and 1. The driver snapshots on begin and restores on rollback. It asserts what the driver saw: the awaited write carried the handle, and the late write carried none. Before the fix: 3 failed, 2 passed, with `expected 'Transaction query already complete' to be 'stored'`. After: 7 passed.
- The full `@objectstack/objectql` `local` project (`vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`, `dist` rebuilt): 401 files, 7817 passed, at `ec20faf27e`. The `repo` project: 1 file, 5 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`: clean, and `check:test-typecheck` reports the ledger held with the new file compiling clean. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood typecheck`: clean. Its `include` is `test/**/*`, which covers the new file.
- eslint, narrowed (`eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the 4 changed paths): the three `.ts` files report 0 errors and 0 warnings. The `.md` changeset matches no configuration. `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.

## Reverse verification and ablation

Both legs were committed first, mutated with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit once, blob changed), rebuilt, and checked with `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` (marker present in `dist/index.js`). Each was restored with `git checkout HEAD`, proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`, rebuilt, and preflight-checked again with `--absent`. A shell `trap` restored on EXIT, INT and TERM.

- **Leg A: the closure removed** (`runOpenedUnit`'s `.finally` no longer clears the entry). Red on both layers: unit 3 failed and 2 passed; dogfood 3 failed and 1 passed. All three late-write pins went red, because the explicit read consults the same entry. The no-transaction control and the joined-unit case stayed green. This was the expected direction.
- **Leg B: the explicit read ablated** (`buildDriverOptions` ignores `isClosedUnitHandle`). Red: the explicit probe and the `engine.transaction()` case, on unit 2 failed and 3 passed, and dogfood 2 failed and 2 passed. The ambient case and the control stayed green, so the two halves are separable. The mutated build's `dts` step failed (`TS6133`, `isClosedUnitHandle` unused). The CJS and ESM bundles the suites consume had already built, and the preflight found the marker in `dist/index.js`, `dist/core.js` and `dist/core.mjs`. The restore build was clean.
- **Leg C: the door predicate removed** (patch round 1; `opensAfterAbortUnit` treats any threaded handle as an open unit again). Red: the door-unit pin, `expected [ +0, +0 ] to deeply equal [ 1, 1 ]` (unit 1 failed and 6 passed). Its no-transaction control and every other case stayed green. The dogfood file has no door-unit case and stayed green (4 passed). Restore proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`; the restore build was clean and `--absent` exited 0.

## Gates (head `ec20faf27e`)

The dispatch's 68-command list and this diff's own derivation (`dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 72 families; the 4 extra are `@objectstack/spec` source audits) come to 72 commands. Every one exited 0 at `ec20faf27e`. `dispatch-gates --ran` reports 72 derived, 72 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED and 0 UNRUN, with every exit code recorded. In this round, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3) in the recreated worktree and went green once its 8 packages were built.

- The first battery, at `f3230fca02`, had two refusals that measured nothing. `check-engine-split-ratio --days 90` exited 2 because the clone was shallow inside its window; it went green after `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-06 origin main`. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3) because 8 unbuilt packages had no `dist/`; it went green once those were built.
- `check:type-check-debt` re-measured its ledger and held, with no entry above its recorded number.

## Acceptance notes

- **The write door's unit for a late write (patch round 1, the seat's ruling A, which lifts the claim's exclusion for this one predicate).** `opensAfterAbortUnit` now reads a threaded handle through the same `isClosedUnitHandle` predicate as `buildDriverOptions`. A late write that carries a closed unit's handle therefore opens the door's own unit exactly when the same write outside any unit would, and an aborting blocking `after*` hook rolls it back. No other change to the door's unit selection. Pinned in the unit file with a no-transaction control, and ablation leg C turns it red.
- `HookContext.transaction` and `ScopedContext.transactionHandle` still expose the raw handle to a late hook. Every engine-routed read and write ignores it once its unit is closed. A handler that hands it to a driver directly is outside the engine.
- Release text: seat 1's note on #22855 said the pending `.changeset/22782-objectql-after-hook-abort-rolls-back.md` sentence about un-awaited work becomes true for `ctx.api.transaction(fn)` once this lands. With patch round 1 it holds in full, the "as it would outside any unit" clause included. That changeset is not edited here.
- `origin/main` is not merged. It is 12 commits ahead; none touch `packages/objectql`. Two touch other dogfood test files and one touches `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, which this diff adds no engine double to. CI's merge ref is the joint check.

## Line budget

423 changed lines (399 additions, 24 deletions) over 4 files (patch round 1 is 54 additions and 14 deletions of those):
- engine source: 72 additions and 24 deletions, mostly the helper's docblock;
- unit pin: 196;
- real-door pin: 115;
- changeset: 16.
